title: How long should a food road remember?
question: Which one is the trail -- which pane lets you follow where the food goes?
context_md:
You asked: ***"is it too much to track actual paths and make trail?"***

**It was never too much, and it was already tracking them.** The road marks the exact cell an ant stands on, every tick it moves. What it was doing wrong is **forgetting** -- it dropped a mark to half in ten seconds, so what reached the screen was the last few hundred steps anybody took, scattered along the surface. One of these panes holds a minute instead. Nothing else differs: same bed, same seed, same run, same animals.

- **red-orange** -- an ant walked here **carrying**
- **blue** -- an ant walked here with nothing
- the harvest map is off in both, so this is the road on its own

**Scrub it.** The trail builds as they work; that is the part a still cannot show.

**And it is free, which I measured before proposing it rather than after.** The longer memory holds nearly four times as much road and costs nothing either instrument can see: on a settled bed, where this view is dearest because it forces a full repaint, the short memory came out **+0.82 ms** a frame over having the view off and the long one **+0.73**; over a whole running frame, **+0.56 ms** against **+0.47**. The check that says the ruler works at all is a second channel drawn on the same bed, which moves the same number to **+1.17 ms**. What this view costs is having it switched on -- not what it remembers.

Whichever you pick becomes the default, and the other stays a dial.
